speaker: AIDEN
text: I went to see Red the morning after the funeral with a bullet in my body and a diamond pin covering the hole in my coat.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank drove. I sat beside him with the note open on my knee.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante didn't die for three million.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The nigga had written it in red ink. He wanted me looking at it all night, wondering what my woman hadn't told me. Nigga, I had done exactly that. I wasn't giving him the pleasure of knowing.

speaker: TANK
text: Nigga, you slept at all?

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank asked.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, I can dream about firing you with my eyes open.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He reached into the console and handed me the little bottle Dr. Vega had left for me.

speaker: TANK
text: Take what she said to take.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, I heard the doctor.

speaker: TANK
text: Then listen to her.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I put the bottle in my pocket. He was wearing black again. The nigga had carried a coffin yesterday and was driving me toward another one today. I looked at his hands on the wheel. There was a cut across his knuckles I didn't remember putting there.

speaker: AIDEN
text: At the Saint, two men approached my door before the valet could. I stepped out holding Red's note.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Your boss sent for me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: One of them put his hand out for my gun.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, you can have the note.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He looked toward the entrance. Red stood inside the glass doors in a cream suit, watching.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He lifted one finger. The men backed off.

speaker: RED
text: Aiden,

speaker: AIDEN
text: he said when I reached him.

speaker: RED
text: Glad you came.

speaker: AIDEN
text: You would've been sad if I didn't?

speaker: RED
text: I had breakfast made.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Then feed a nigga before the conversation gets hungry.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He put his arm around me like we were cousins. I let him. Nigga, I wanted to know how close this motherfucker would come to a man who had killed his friend.

speaker: AIDEN
text: My nigga came close enough to squeeze my shoulder.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Before the waiters brought the food, Red took me past the white piano.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Slowly. Nigga wanted me to inspect the flowers, the polished lid, the photograph of Shawna singing on his wall. He paused beneath the picture until I looked. Then he waited for me to dislike looking.

speaker: RED
text: "You play?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga, is breakfast behind the piano?"

speaker: RED
text: "I wondered what you brought to a woman who already sings."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank closed his eyes.

speaker: TANK
text: "Please,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: my nigga said quietly.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "You want a request?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: "I want eggs before the niggas serving them retire."

speaker: AIDEN
text: I sat down. There was sheet music on the stand, Shawna's name written at the top. A long introduction, crowded voices, enough work for both hands that Red had clearly expected me to shut the lid after looking.

speaker: RED
text: "That's a difficult arrangement,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: he said.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga, we haven't heard your kitchen yet. Everything difficult until somebody does it."

speaker: AIDEN
text: My first chord stopped the nearest waiter. I kept going. My fingers remembered a church piano, an old woman's hand correcting my wrist, free suppers I earned by staying to play after everybody else went home.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red had bought a roomful of reminders. Nigga forgot I came with my own.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I played the introduction straight through. Then I brought the melody into my right hand and gave the left something uglier to say about the man standing behind me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank opened his eyes.

speaker: TANK
text: "Oh, this nigga."

speaker: RED
text: "Something wrong?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red asked.

speaker: TANK
text: "With him? All morning. With that? Listen."

speaker: AIDEN
text: The waiter holding the coffee pot shifted his weight in time. Caught himself. Stopped. His foot kept going.

speaker: RED
text: "You just read that?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red asked.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga, you left it open."

speaker: RED
text: "Shawna never said—"

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga, you want me to play or collect witness statements?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: The man at the door laughed. Red turned. The nigga straightened so fast I almost missed a note enjoying it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I finished. The last chord stayed in the room while I took my hands away.

speaker: AIDEN
text: One waiter clapped once. Looked at Red. Looked at me. Then, fuck it, that brave nigga clapped again. The others joined him.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank spread his hands toward the piano.

speaker: TANK
text: "You ordered that,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: he told Red.

speaker: TANK
text: "Nigga asked him what he brought. He unpacked."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red looked at Shawna's photograph.

speaker: RED
text: "She never mentioned you played."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "I keep giving her things to find out."

speaker: AIDEN
text: I closed the lid gently. Nigga, I'd embarrass the owner before I'd damage his instrument.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "You ought to try it."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank caught my elbow when I stood, before my side could spoil the exit.

speaker: TANK
text: "Breakfast,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: he said.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga, you hungry?"

speaker: TANK
text: "I've lived two years since we parked."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Upstairs, the penthouse had been cleaned since Shawna and I left it. He led us through to a terrace where six waiters stood around a table set for three. There were roses in tall crystal vases. My nigga had put the only red one in front of me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank picked it up.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Don't eat that,

speaker: AIDEN
text: I said.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He looked at me.

speaker: TANK
text: I wasn't going to eat it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red laughed. He had little dimples when he laughed. Nigga, I hated them immediately.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I sat. The chair hurt my side, so I moved. Red watched that too.

speaker: RED
text: T always did know where to put a bullet.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, he didn't know where to keep his own.

speaker: AIDEN
text: One of the waiters stopped pouring.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red raised his orange juice.

speaker: RED
text: To our absent friend.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I drank water. My nigga Tank didn't touch anything.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red ate as if he'd invited us to discuss a vacation. He offered Tank bacon. Tank took some, then looked pissed at himself for doing it.

speaker: RED
text: Where's Shawna?

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red asked.

speaker: AIDEN
text: With people who like her alive.

speaker: RED
text: I've always liked her alive.

speaker: AIDEN
text: You got an expensive way of showing it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He put his fork down.

speaker: RED
text: I bought her the dress she was wearing when you met her.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I leaned forward too fast. Pain burned all the way through my side, but I kept my face still.

speaker: AIDEN
text: You want me to send you the motherfucking dress?

speaker: RED
text: I want you to understand how little of this you understand.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, that's the first time you said anything all morning.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He smiled again.

speaker: RED
text: I gave her a room when Valentino died. I protected her from people who would've cut her life short over what she did to him. Then my partner arranges to take her and three million dollars out of my house. My partner dies. You inherit his business, his car, his necklace, and the woman. That's a very fortunate week.

speaker: AIDEN
text: You forgot the bullet.

speaker: RED
text: No. I can see you haven't.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank's chair scraped. I raised my hand without looking at my nigga.

speaker: AIDEN
text: You think I planned that shit?

speaker: AIDEN
text: I asked.

speaker: RED
text: I think you're young enough to be honest when it profits you.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Then here's some honesty. Send another nigga after her, I'll come back without an invitation.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red wiped his mouth. He was thirty-six years old and had men older than his father standing around waiting to refill his fucking juice. Nigga, I could feel the kind of money he had. It made the air colder.

speaker: RED
text: You can keep T's streets,

speaker: AIDEN
text: he said.

speaker: RED
text: That's a generous beginning.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I can keep what's already mine? Damn. Put a bow on it.

speaker: RED
text: The money comes back. Shawna comes home. We stop putting people in the ground.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Which people you want me to bring back? T? Dante? Valentino? You got a favorite?

speaker: AIDEN
text: He stopped smiling at Dante's name.

speaker: AIDEN
text: There it was.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I sat back and let the pain take its time through me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: You wrote me a note,

speaker: AIDEN
text: I said.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Finish it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red looked at the waiters. They left. He waited until the last door shut before he spoke.

speaker: RED
text: Eight years ago, I bought something extraordinary from a man who didn't appreciate the opportunity he'd been given.

speaker: AIDEN
text: What man?

speaker: RED
text: Marcellus Vale. A jeweler. Violent when disappointed.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank's hand tightened around his glass.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red saw it. The nigga saw everything except the day somebody would finally kill him.

speaker: RED
text: His masterpiece was called Blue Mercy. Large blue diamond. Depending on who's asking, somewhere around forty million dollars.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, I had been pretending all morning that nothing could surprise me. Forty million surprised the absolute fuck out of me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, forty million for one rock?

speaker: RED
text: One.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, for forty million that bitch better call me when I'm lonely.

speaker: RED
text: It has made quite a few men lonely.

speaker: AIDEN
text: What does Dante got to do with it?

speaker: RED
text: Dante met Vale in prison. Came home with some unfortunate ideas. Decided the money in my accounts belonged to a woman he'd never met.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Which woman got that nigga reaching into your accounts?

speaker: RED
text: Vale's dead wife.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red picked up his glass again.

speaker: RED
text: Men do peculiar things when they love dead women. It's why I advise you to avoid the habit.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I stood up. Tank stood with me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, you can tell me what you know about Dante, or you can keep talking about my woman until this breakfast gets real fucking expensive.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red didn't move.

speaker: RED
text: Shawna knows the story.

speaker: AIDEN
text: No.

speaker: RED
text: Ask her.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I fucking did.

speaker: RED
text: Then ask her again.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He pushed an envelope across the table. Inside were two invitations, heavy blue paper edged in silver.

speaker: RED
text: The diamond will be the centerpiece of my gala in three nights. I thought Shawna might like to see what her husband died chasing.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I looked at the invitation. Her name was printed before mine.

speaker: AIDEN
text: You printed these before the funeral?

speaker: RED
text: I print a lot of invitations.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, print one for yours.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank touched my elbow. I pulled away because I wanted Red to know nobody in that room could move me except me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: We got to the door before Red spoke again.

speaker: RED
text: Tell her I still have the piano.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I turned.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He was cutting into his breakfast.

speaker: RED
text: The white one. She'll know.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, I went back across the terrace, took his untouched vase of roses, and threw it over the railing.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Glass broke somewhere far below. A woman screamed.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red rose halfway out of his chair.

speaker: RED
text: That's my fucking car.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tell it I still have the vase.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I put the wet broken stem I was holding on his plate and left.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red's car was a red Aston Martin, and the vase had gone through the roof of it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The valet stood beside it holding a towel. I didn't know what the towel was going to solve. The entire car looked like an expensive mouth that had bitten into glass.

speaker: B01C06_VALET
text: "Mr. Red is going to be upset,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: he said.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga, he got a head start upstairs. Where's mine?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank went to the Mercedes. They had replaced its windows since our first night, repaired the back, polished it until I could see myself coming. I loved that car. It kept surviving my life without asking me to slow it down.

speaker: AIDEN
text: A man came out of the next hotel carrying a helmet under one arm. He saw the car, then me, then the broken Aston Martin.

speaker: LITTLE_SAINT
text: "You Aiden?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Depends who's hoping."

speaker: LITTLE_SAINT
text: "Nigga, you flew over a boat."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Word getting around."

speaker: AIDEN
text: He grinned. Thirty-one, brown skin, a scar down his chin, leather jacket with a silver eagle on the back. He pointed across the drive at a black motorcycle that looked ready to leave without him.

speaker: LITTLE_SAINT
text: "Name's Saint. Everybody calls me Little Saint. I ride."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Good for you."

speaker: LITTLE_SAINT
text: "I mean I ride. Thought maybe you should know that."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank opened my door.

speaker: TANK
text: "Everybody got something they want this nigga to know today."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Little Saint's smile disappeared as he looked past us.

speaker: LITTLE_SAINT
text: "Then know those two cars ain't valets."

speaker: AIDEN
text: A gray sports car had stopped across the exit. Behind it a black SUV rolled forward with its windows coming down. The man in the front passenger seat held a pistol against his chest. He wasn't wearing the Saint's colors. He wasn't wearing anything that told me whether he loved T or hated me or had been paid enough to do both.

speaker: TANK
text: "Inside,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank said.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The first bullet hit the Mercedes door while his hand was still on it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I grabbed the valet by his collar and threw him behind the car. Glass burst from the hotel's revolving door. People dropped behind luggage and flowerpots. Little Saint ran for his motorcycle, helmet swinging from his hand, and the SUV's engine roared toward us.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank fired from beside my shoulder. I got into the passenger seat as he came around the hood. The Mercedes lurched back before his door was shut.

speaker: AIDEN
text: We hit the gray car hard enough to move it sideways. Its driver shouted through the window. Tank hit it again. The gap opened, and we came through with sparks sliding along my door.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga, somebody really hates breakfast,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: I said.

speaker: TANK
text: "Put your head down."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "I need it where I can see."

speaker: TANK
text: "Then see lower."

speaker: AIDEN
text: The gray car came after us. Its front fender hung loose, slapping the wheel every time it turned. The SUV stayed farther back, its passenger firing through the missing window.

speaker: AIDEN
text: We took the first corner too fast. A taxi braked across our path. Tank turned, missed its front bumper by inches, and put us into a narrow street lined with parked delivery trucks.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The gray car followed. The SUV couldn't make the turn cleanly and struck a streetlight. I heard metal break behind us. The nigga kept coming anyway.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Little Saint appeared beside us on the motorcycle.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He was laughing.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Not because he didn't understand. The nigga understood perfectly. Somebody had finally made his morning worth wearing the jacket for.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He pointed ahead. A tour bus stood across the next intersection. Its driver was outside arguing with a man in a yellow vest. Neither had seen us.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Tank!"

speaker: TANK
text: "I see it!"

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga, I keep hearing that right before we hit something!"

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank braked. The Mercedes slid. Behind us the gray car tried to stop and couldn't. Its nose struck our rear quarter, spinning us halfway around.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Now I was looking straight at it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The driver looked straight at me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: For one second we shared the intimate knowledge that his nigga had chosen the wrong car to pursue.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I fired through the broken rear window. His windshield bloomed white. He ducked, lost the turn, and struck the tour bus's empty luggage compartment with the whole front of his car.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The bus driver dropped his argument and ran.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank put us into the gap beside the bus. The Mercedes scraped along its side. I could see luggage stacked behind a little square window, somebody's pink suitcase shaking every time our car hit another panel.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Then we came out into open road.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Little Saint was still beside us. He raised a fist. I raised mine back.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The SUV hit him.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Not square. Its bumper caught the motorcycle's back wheel as it tried to pass. The bike snapped sideways. Little Saint flew off, rolling across the hood of a parked car and down into the street.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank swore.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I had the door open before he stopped.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga, where the fuck—"

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Get him!"

speaker: AIDEN
text: I ran across the road. The SUV turned toward us. I could see its driver watching me, smiling the same fucking smile every man wore when he thought my love for somebody had finally made me easy to kill.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Little Saint was on one elbow trying to stand. His helmet had cracked. Blood ran down his cheek. He looked up at me like he couldn't believe I'd come back.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Your leg?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: I asked.

speaker: LITTLE_SAINT
text: "Works."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Then work it with me."

speaker: AIDEN
text: I pulled him up. We ran for the parked cars together while the SUV came at our backs. Tank's Mercedes surged across its path. The two cars struck, and the sound filled the street.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I pushed Little Saint behind a truck and turned with my gun up.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The SUV had stopped against the Mercedes. Its driver tried to open his door. Tank came out of his own car like the crash had merely rung a bell for him. He caught the door, slammed it back, and hauled the driver through the window instead.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I covered the passenger until he dropped his gun.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga, you can keep breathing,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: I told him.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "That's all you getting from me today."

speaker: AIDEN
text: He put both hands on the dashboard.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Little Saint stood behind me with his jacket torn at the shoulder. He stared at Tank, then at me, then at the smoking cars.

speaker: LITTLE_SAINT
text: "You came back."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "You told me you ride. I ain't seen enough yet."

speaker: AIDEN
text: His face changed. The grin came back slower this time, carrying something heavier underneath it.

speaker: LITTLE_SAINT
text: "Any road,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: he said.

speaker: LITTLE_SAINT
text: "Any fucking road, Aiden. You call, I'm there."

speaker: AIDEN
text: A crowd had gathered at the corner. Somebody shouted my name. A woman held up her phone and asked me to look toward her. I did, because nigga, if they were going to put me on every screen in Vegas they could at least get the good side.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Knox's officers arrived before the smoke stopped. They recognized me immediately. One of them looked at the wrecked SUV and shook his head with open wonder.

speaker: B01C06_OFFICER
text: "Chief said you were something."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Chief been paying attention."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Tank made a call. Another car came for Little Saint. Our Mercedes still ran, because some machines knew who they belonged to and refused to embarrass him.

speaker: AIDEN
text: We drove home with one door tied shut by a belt and the whole street watching us leave.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I called Shawna before we reached the highway.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Baby, you want lunch?"

speaker: SHAWNA
text: "Why are there sirens behind you?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Niggas wanted breakfast. I'm thinking ahead."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna was at the house with Rosa, standing barefoot on a little platform while a woman pinned a dress around her hips. The dress was silver, and I wanted every nigga out of the fucking room so I could look at her properly.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Then I saw the watch on her wrist.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante's watch. Dante's wife. Dante's fucking diamond.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I had bought the house by the water. I had bled in the car getting her here. Somehow the dead man was still first through every door.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Rosa looked up.

speaker: ROSA
text: Why you got that face?

speaker: AIDEN
text: What face?

speaker: ROSA
text: The one that's going to make this dress cost more.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I held up the invitations.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Blue Mercy.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna stopped moving.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The woman kneeling beside her kept working until Rosa put a hand on her shoulder.

speaker: ROSA
text: Let's get coffee,

speaker: AIDEN
text: Rosa said.

speaker: B01C06_DRESS_FITTER
text: I don't drink coffee,

speaker: AIDEN
text: the woman said.

speaker: ROSA
text: Today's a good fucking day to start.

speaker: AIDEN
text: They left us alone.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna stepped down from the platform. A pin fell out of the dress and landed between us.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: What did he tell you?

speaker: AIDEN
text: I laughed once. It sounded ugly in that room.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, everybody keeps asking me that. What did she tell you? What did he tell you? What the fuck did the dead man tell the other dead man? How about you tell me something for once?

speaker: AIDEN
text: She drew back.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I hated that I had made her do it. I kept going anyway.

speaker: AIDEN
text: You knew about forty million dollars?

speaker: SHAWNA
text: I knew about the stone.

speaker: AIDEN
text: And you didn't think that shit mattered?

speaker: SHAWNA
text: I thought you being shot mattered. I thought getting you through yesterday mattered.

speaker: AIDEN
text: You got time to pick a fucking dress, Shawna.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Her face changed.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: I picked this dress because I wanted one night where you looked at me and didn't see somebody else bleeding.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I didn't have anything ready for that.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She took the invitation out of my hand. Her thumb went over Red's name.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: He told you about his piano?

speaker: AIDEN
text: Yeah, he told me about the piano. He tell everybody about the piano?

speaker: SHAWNA
text: I smashed the keys with a bottle the night I left. He bought another one so he could pretend I was coming back.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He said you knew what Dante died for.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: I know what Dante told me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Then tell me.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: It starts before me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, everything in this house starts before me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She looked down at the cross against my shirt.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: You want me to take that back?

speaker: AIDEN
text: My hand closed around it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: No.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: Then sit down, Aiden.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: Dante told me after we got married,

speaker: AIDEN
text: she said.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: We were in the room Red paid for. I thought we'd go downstairs and drink with everybody. He locked the door instead.

speaker: AIDEN
text: My nigga, I felt my jaw tighten.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I'm listening.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: He said there was something I ought to know before I decided what kind of man I'd married.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She took my hand off the cross and held it.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: Then he told me about the old man.
